paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. A nation that looks like it has everything still ends up in God's hands. The people of Cush were tall, widely feared and powerful, and their couriers were out on the waters in papyrus vessels (Isaiah 18:2). But the LORD says, "I will quietly look on from My dwelling place…" (Isaiah 18:4), and quiet doesn't mean absent or asleep.

Think about what that means for you. Plenty of us watch the powerful and think they're running the show. The passage says that before the harvest, He is the One who cuts off the shoots with a pruning knife (Isaiah 18:5). So when the loud, scary people of this world get your attention, remember who is quietly watching them.

Now hold on, because the ending is the part I love. After all that woe, "gifts will be brought to the LORD of Hosts" from that very same feared nation, to Mount Zion (Isaiah 18:7). The people who started out under a warning end up bringing gifts to Him. So pray for the people who scare you, baker, because God's plans for them can end somewhere beautiful.
